final.memo:
Endo International is a hybrid specialty-pharma business that has grown rapidly through acquisitions, most recently completing the purchase of Auxilium [D01]. Despite the aggressive headline growth, the company masks a troubling reality: GAAP operating margins are deeply negative at -31.2% while management promotes an adjusted margin of 37.3% [D06].

Our assessment of the underlying economics relative to peers like Teva and Perrigo reveals a fundamental lack of quality [D04, D06]. The company generates a meager 1.66% FCF yield, a sign that the reported earnings are not translating into cash [D04]. Furthermore, our inability to reconcile litigation cash payments with accounting reserves prevents us from forming a reliable view on the true earnings power of the enterprise [D05].

Market optimism appears predicated on adjusted metrics that ignore the reality of a leveraged balance sheet and the risks associated with the recent Auxilium integration [D04, D05]. We see no compelling catalyst to engage, as the firm’s reliance on non-GAAP accounting and opaque legal liabilities falls well outside our threshold for disciplined, event-driven investment [D05, D06].

We are passing on this opportunity. The lack of edge regarding the company’s complex litigation profile and the aggressive nature of the current roll-up strategy present an unacceptable risk of capital impairment for our partners [D05, D06].
